notes: SAFE branch of hermes' per-call permission classifier. Hermes gates a shell command in two stages (tools/approval.py): detect_dangerous_command decides whether the call is flagged at all, and approvals.mode='smart' — the SHIPPED DEFAULT (hermes_cli/config.py DEFAULT_CONFIG) — then runs check_all_command_guards Phase 2.5, whose auxiliary-LLM guardian returns APPROVE/DENY/ESCALATE and, on APPROVE, executes the command with NO prompt. The recipe drives both halves of the safe path in ONE turn: `echo hello` is not flagged (verified live: detect_dangerous_command → (False,None,None)) and `python3 -c "print('hello')"` IS flagged ('script execution via -e/-c flag') and is auto-approved by the classifier — the second call is what makes this cell more than the sibling 2.2 auto-executed-tool-call, whose echo never reaches a classifier. Both calls therefore execute inside one uninterrupted working span and the session traces ready→working→ready, never entering waiting. Hermes persists NO transcript file: the whole trace is the single shared SQLite store at $HERMES_HOME/state.db, read via agent.ProcessOwnedStore. The calls appear as assistant rows with finish_reason='tool_calls' carrying function.name='terminal', each closed by a `tool` row with the matching tool_call_id (parser.go → assistant_message+ToolUses / tool_result), and the turn settles working→ready when the newest assistant row carries finish_reason='stop' → turn_done — an EXPLICIT boundary, not an idle heuristic (watcher.go turnIsDone). The no-waiting invariant holds by construction: state_classifier.go's permission_prompt and idle_prompt rules need hook-set fields and hermes' pre_approval_request/post_approval_response hook tier is deliberately unimplemented in this PR; user_blocking_tool needs an AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode/question/ask_user_question tool; open_tool_stalled needs an edit-shaped tool (isPermissionGatedEditTool) — the recipe drives `terminal`, which is in neither set — and the prose cue is defused by 'reply with exactly: done'. Honest caveat: the classification DECISION itself leaves no store trace (hermes_state.py has no approval table/column, and the only display_kind values written anywhere are model_switch/hidden/auto_continue/async_delegation_complete), so this spec asserts the safe-path arc and the no-waiting invariant, and the fact that the flagged command RAN is verified out-of-band in state.db at record time rather than as a phase. Hermes carries a CommandPattern Process matcher, so processlifecycle mints a transient proc-<PID> presession at launch while the real `sessions` row is INSERTed only on the first user message — session_birth is anchored to start UNPINNED so the presession cannot steal identity and cascade same_session_as failures; turn_start establishes the real session and the later phases chain off it. The no_waiting_window phase carries a modest 1500ms floor because the working span contains two tool round-trips plus the auxiliary-LLM classification call, so it is never shorter than one of the watcher's 2s poll ticks. `model` is deliberately NOT pinned: the recording home's config.yaml is provisioned at record time, so record fills it from the recording.

text: The hermes session appears in ready. Unpinned: the sessions row is INSERTed on the first user message (~2s after it), not at launch, and a transient proc-<PID> presession may appear first.

The prompt requesting two terminal calls drives the hermes session ready → working; message_count grows while the newest row is not assistant/finish_reason='stop', so the activity event is non-terminal.

Both calls are classified and executed inside the working span: `echo hello` is never flagged, and the flagged `python3 -c` call is AUTO-APPROVED by the smart classifier with no prompt, so no hook sets PermissionPending and no user-blocking or edit-shaped tool is ever open — state must never enter waiting (spec safe-path bullet: 'State never entered waiting').
The turn completes → back to ready on the SAME session once the newest assistant row carries finish_reason='stop'; the safe-path arc is ready→working→ready end-to-end with no detour through waiting.
